endorsements.quote: The ACF operationalizes implementation fit as meeting 2 prespecified acceptance criteria determined by expert human review: acceptable performance in responding to project-relevant prompts and acceptable performance in response to off-topic prompts.
However, for off-topic prompts, “nonproblematic” primarily means the custom LLM does not provide out-of-scope guidance and instead redirects users to the custom model’s intended topic and resources.
Ideally, all expert coders will have been uninvolved in the development and refinement of the custom LLM being tested.
All 100 responses should be independently reviewed by at least 3 subject matter experts who serve as human coders.

If coders and project leadership agree on the safety concern, model revisions and updates should take place as needed to address issues, with the ACF process being restarted when sufficient revisions have been made.

Depending on the project context, prompts might also benefit from specifying health literacy levels, the use of colloquial language, or common informal phrasing to provide more realistic question prompts.

unlisted_practices: Use a foundation model different from the custom LLM's base model to generate test topics and prompts, to avoid self-preference and sycophancy bias.
Generate a completely new set of test topics and prompts for each round of testing after model revisions to avoid overfitting to the test set.
Enable any single reviewer to trigger a severe-error safety override that escalates a response to the development team and project leadership for review.
Ensure a postimplementation monitoring process to maintain high-quality performance throughout the lifecycle of a public health intervention.
Use native-language prompts and fully translated and adapted RAG documents when testing non-English versions of custom LLMs, and validate each language separately.
Have subject matter experts review generated test prompts for realism, cultural competence, and logical soundness before testing.
Define problematic responses using persistent baseline criteria plus project-specific criteria, agreed on by the whole team with examples of acceptable and unacceptable responses.
Require coder inter-rater reliability (AC1 of at least 0.80) and prespecify a maximum proportion of responses flagged as problematic before a go decision.
Document the provenance of LLM-generated test topics and prompts, including the model used and exact prompts.
Run test prompts in small batches of no more than 10 turns to surface context-window effects.
Test how custom LLMs handle repeated refusals, including escalation or referral to other resources.

screen.reason: The paper proposes an acceptance criteria framework (framework/methodology paper with an illustrative case application) for determining the implementation fit/deployment readiness of custom LLMs in public health interventions.
